# Public settable auto-properties in Majorsilence.Forms that nothing in the assembly ever
# reads the value of -- set by application code, readable back, consumed by no code here.
# A property counts as consumed if its getter is called OR its backing field is read
# somewhere other than that getter. See StoredOnlyPropertyBaselineTests and
# docs/behaviour-gap-plan.md (RC-7).
#
# The entries below ARE the count; the denominator is deliberately not recorded here.
# It moved on every merge, which made this header collide with every open branch and
# turned a generated file into a source of hand-resolved conflicts. A live number was
# never the right thing to keep here: dated snapshots of it belong in
# docs/behaviour-gap-plan.md, which quotes them per item, and the current entry count
# is whatever `grep -vc '^#\|^$'` on this file says.
#
# This is a list of facts, not a to-do list. Some entries are legitimately inert (`Tag` is
# app storage; the Win32 shell extras have no portable meaning) -- when that is the case,
# say so beside the entry rather than removing it.
#
# Absence from this file does NOT mean the property works: a property read only by code
# that is itself inert counts as consumed here. ComboBox.IntegralHeight and
# ComboBox.DropDownHeight are both absent and neither does anything -- their only readers
# are ToolStripComboBox's pass-through wrappers, which forward and nothing more. The three
# examples this note used to give (ListView.View, TextBox.WordWrap, TextBox.AcceptsReturn)
# have since been fixed by W5.6, W5.11 and Phase 1, which is the other half of the point:
# an entry's absence here says nothing either way. See StoredOnlyPropertyBaselineTests for
# why, and docs/behaviour-gap/ for that class of finding.
#
# Auto-properties only: a property with hand-written accessors is invisible here, so the
# real figure is higher.
# Regenerate with MAJORSILENCE_WRITE_STORED_ONLY_BASELINE=1.
